questions.q: What is SOX primarily designed to ensure, per this lesson?
options: The accuracy of public companies' financial reports and the trustworthiness of the controls behind them
That all companies, public and private, encrypt customer personal data
That healthcare providers protect patient health information
That European Union residents' personal data is handled lawfully
questions.explain: SOX was passed after accounting scandals like Enron and WorldCom to ensure publicly traded companies' financial reports are accurate and their internal controls can be trusted — it is not a privacy law.

Companies to notify regulators of a data breach within 72 hours
Consumers to be given the right to opt out of data sales
Healthcare providers to appoint a privacy officer
questions.explain: Section 302 requires corporate officers, typically the CEO and CFO, to personally certify that the company's financial reports are accurate.

questions.q: What does SOX Section 404 require, and what body did SOX create to add independent oversight?
options: Management's assessment of internal controls plus auditor attestation; SOX created the PCAOB to oversee audits of public companies
A single annual password reset for all employees; SOX created the CPPA
Mandatory encryption of all emails; SOX created the FTC
A ban on all third-party auditors; SOX created the SEC
questions.explain: Section 404 requires management to assess internal controls over financial reporting, with the company's independent auditor attesting to that assessment. SOX also established the PCAOB to oversee audits of public companies.

questions.q: Which of these correctly matches a named sector-specific rule to the data category it protects, per this lesson?
options: PCI DSS protects payment card data
FERPA protects financial-services customer data
GLBA protects student education records
PCI DSS protects student education records
questions.explain: PCI DSS is the industry-mandated standard for organizations handling payment card data. GLBA covers financial-services customer information, and FERPA covers student education records.

questions.q: Why does this lesson treat SOX as a data governance topic even though it is not a privacy law?
options: Because Section 404's internal-controls requirement is, in practice, a data integrity and access-control requirement — exactly the kind of work data governance supports
Because SOX directly regulates personal data of EU residents
Because SOX replaced GDPR for publicly traded companies
Because SOX requires the same 72-hour breach notification as GDPR
questions.explain: SOX never mentions 'data governance,' but demonstrating accurate, access-controlled, auditable financial data to satisfy Section 404 is precisely the infrastructure a data governance program builds.
